title: Petlibro accused of “gaslighting” users over smart pet feeder outage
gist: A multi-day cloud-server outage left Petlibro smart pet feeders uncontrollable via app, and the China-owned firm faces accusations of downplaying the incident and of feeders failing to run scheduled offline feedings—highlighting cloud-dependency risk in IoT consumer devices.

insights.claim: A cloud-server backlog overloaded system memory and repeatedly brought down Petlibro's device service, leaving users unable to control smart feeders via the app and in some reported cases with hungry pets.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Illustrates single-point cloud-failure risk in connected consumer hardware—reputational and reliability exposure for IoT vendors.
insights.quote: The outage was due to cloud server issues that caused a backlog of data requests, overloading the system memory and bringing down device service

insights.claim: Petlibro claims feeders run pre-scheduled feedings offline independent of the app, but multiple users reported this failed during the outage, fueling accusations the company was 'gaslighting' customers.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Trust erosion over crisis communications is a churn risk; smart-device buyers increasingly scrutinize offline-functionality claims.
